extracted.intended_audience: inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) administrators, clinicians, quality staff, and measure developers/stakeholders responding to CMS IRF QRP rules
extracted.subtask_short: IRF SDOH assessment and QRP measures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule decisions on standardized SDOH assessment items (Living Situation, Food, Utilities, Transportation), timing and coding of data collection, candidate quality measure concepts for the IRF QRP, and principles for an IRF star rating system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt four new SDOH assessment items
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt four new items as standardized patient assessment data elements under the SDOH category beginning with the FY 2028 IRF QRP: one Living Situation item; two Food items; and one Utilities item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized after public comment; draft items available in IRF-PAI downloads. Collection to begin for patients admitted on October 1, 2026 for purposes of the FY 2028 QRP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify Transportation item to align with AHC HRSN Screening Tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the current A1250. Transportation item in the IRF-PAI so that it aligns with the Transportation item collected on the AHC HRSN Screening Tool (adapted from PRAPARE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adapted item asks, “In the past 12 months, has a lack of reliable transportation kept you from medical appointments, meetings, work or from getting things needed for daily living?” Alignment is intended to improve standardization across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation look-back period: 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a defined 12-month look back period for the Transportation assessment item rather than a 6–12 month or 3-month look back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: a 12-month look back reduces ambiguity, improves validity, and accounts for fluctuating transportation needs over time. CMS disagrees with commenters recommending a 3-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplified Transportation response options
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simplified response options for the Transportation item consistent with AHC: (0) Yes; (1) No; (7) Patient declines to respond; (8) Patient unable to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces previously separate options for medical vs non-medical transportation to reduce administrative burden and improve ease of answering; CMS will develop coding guidance using comment feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect new SDOH items at admission only
rubrics_metrics.description: Require IRFs to collect and submit the Living Situation, Food, and Utilities items (and the modified Transportation item) at admission only beginning October 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS finds admission-only collection reasonable because these item responses are unlikely to differ at discharge; IRFs that collect at admission only will be deemed to have collected at discharge as well. Evidence showed only a 0.19 percentage point difference in Transportation responses admission vs discharge in analyzed data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain interim collection of current Transportation for care coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to collect the current Transportation assessment item in the interim (through September 30, 2025) if finalized, for care coordination and discharge planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites CFR 482.43(a) and the need for ongoing information during the transition to the modified item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture comprehensive utility services
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities assessment item should capture utility needs across electric, gas, oil, and water services to understand patients' access to necessary utility services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes patients' needs for utilities may vary depending on equipment needs at discharge and will use comment feedback to develop coding guidance; response options should address patient declines or inability to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRFs may screen for additional HRSNs
rubrics_metrics.description: Although IRF-PAI requires collection of certain HRSNs, IRFs may screen for additional health-related social needs they believe relevant for their patient population and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: collecting details on water access or voltage capacity if relevant to discharge planning; additional screening may inform care and discharge planning beyond standardized items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable flexibility in collection method but require coding consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: IRFs may use different methods to collect SDOH assessment items so long as they are consistent with coding guidance and defined lookback periods in the IRF-PAI manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS clarifies that these items will be collected through the IRF-PAI and do not mandate the use of a new vendor tool; flexibility is permitted on how/when data are gathered, but coding rules and lookback periods must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer patient interview ('hearing the patient's voice') for SDOH data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS prefers obtaining SDOH information directly from the patient via interview rather than relying on data collected in prior healthcare settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: direct patient interview is more reliable and accurate—avoids uncertainty about whether prior data were collected from the patient or a proxy, variations in SDOH definitions across settings, and changes/resolutions since prior collection; asking at admission may prompt care planning discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not allow skipping Utilities when homeless (CMS position)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested coding logic to skip the Utilities item if a patient has no steady place to live; CMS disagrees with making Utilities skippable for those without stable housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS stated it is not inappropriate to ask about utilities even if a patient does not have a place to live and will require collection of the Utilities item to have complete information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting schedule for adoption and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: IRFs required to report new/modified items using the IRF-PAI beginning with patients admitted October 1, 2026 (FY 2028 IRF QRP); starting in CY 2027, IRFs must collect and submit data for the entire calendar year for FY 2029 reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft items are available in IRF-PAI downloads; CMS will issue coding guidance before implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future IRF QRP measure concepts under consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS solicited feedback on three candidate measure concepts for future IRF QRP development: a Vaccination Composite, Pain Management, and Depression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concepts were discussed with a Technical Expert Panel and through an RFI; CMS will consider public feedback in future measure development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vaccination Composite considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders raised support and concerns for adding a composite vaccination measure similar to the Adult Immunization Status (AIS) measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns include suitability for IRFs (short stays, contraindications), difficulty verifying vaccination status across multiple providers, data validity (age groups, dose schedules), administrative burden, and whether the measure reflects IRF quality; commenters suggested reporting specific vaccine rates rather than a composite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pain management measure design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: If developed, pain management measures should reflect the full spectrum of recommended pain management interventions (including nonpharmacologic), consider patient-reported outcomes, and measure staff responsiveness to pain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters cautioned against measures that imply an expectation of pain improvement (which could incentivize overprescribing opioids) and suggested leveraging existing IRF-PAI pain interference items or PROMs to avoid additional data collection burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depression measure considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Depression was supported as a concept; commenters suggested using PHQ-2 to PHQ-9 screening and follow-up, and not excluding patients with prior depression/bipolar diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns include redundancy with existing IRF-PAI depression screening questions, resource implications for IRFs (availability of behavioral health treatment), and conflation of PTSD with clinical depression; CMS should assess resource availability before implementing such a measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other suggested measure concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters suggested additional future measure concepts: management of degenerative cognitive conditions, effectiveness of disposition planning and care transitions, changes in patient function, rates of follow-up care, access to appropriate treatments and medications, and inclusion of PAM®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will take these suggestions into consideration for future measure development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for selecting measures for an IRF star rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures chosen for a potential IRF star rating should be patient-centered, representative of IRFs' emphasis on functional outcomes and treating pain, clinically relevant and effective (e.g., prevention of adverse events/readmissions, discharge to home, weaning from supports), and allow meaningful comparisons among IRFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters emphasized the importance of representativeness, clinical relevance, and comparability; CMS should consider these when selecting measures for a star rating scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to avoid in IRF star rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Several commenters recommended against including certain measures (e.g., Falls with Major Injury, CAUTI) in an IRF star rating due to inconsistency with IRF clinical guidelines or lack of meaningful performance differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoiding measures that do not meaningfully distinguish IRF performance or conflict with IRF clinical practice is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation principles for IRF star ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting an IRF star rating, CMS should engage patients, caregivers, providers, and specialty societies; ensure full transparency of the star ratings methodology; and present clear, concise visualizations accompanied by contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualizations should help consumers make informed decisions; stakeholder engagement and methodology transparency were emphasized by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access and feedback to IRFs
rubrics_metrics.description: IRFs should receive timely access to their submitted data and additional feedback reports to support quality improvement; commenters recommended quarterly feedback for claims-based measures and shortening the time between data submission and public reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely feedback helps IRFs identify improvement areas; CMS currently provides similar hospital-level feedback and should consider analogous access for IRFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement development considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adopting new composite or other measures, CMS should evaluate the reliability, validity, and effectiveness of existing measures, consider administrative burden, and account for factors that differentiate IRFs (case mix, payer mix, staffing, accreditation standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended learning from other star rating programs and allowing sufficient time for development; consider accounting for structural indicators (e.g., PM&R physicians, staffing levels, CARF accreditation) in assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns about star rating feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters raised that low IRF volumes and limited numbers of IRF quality measures could make developing a meaningful five-star system and reportability challenging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS should consider volume and data sufficiency issues when designing a star-rating methodology and may need additional measures or alternative approaches for low-volume IRFs.
